fixes.explanation: I can see why you'd say that. Grabbing a cloak sounds reasonable. But Jesus says, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” So the answer is False. The person in the field doesn't go back for it.

Autumn gets my vote for coziest oven weather, baker, but it isn't on Jesus' list. He says, “Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.” Winter is the season He names, so that's the one to remember.
That's the opposite of what Jesus says. He says, “But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.” Shortened, baker, not stretched.

It's actually False, friend. Jesus says false Christs and false prophets “…will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” So they WILL perform signs and wonders. And Jesus adds, “See, I have told you in advance.”

Not the Pharisees, friend. Jesus says the signs and wonders are “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” The elect are the ones He names here. Good thing it's right there in the text, baker.

The scribes aren't named in this verse, friend. Jesus says the signs and wonders are “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” So the elect are the answer. Check the verse and it points right to them.
That's not what Jesus says, baker. He says, “the stars will fall from the sky…” Falling, not brightening. That's the line to hold onto.
Not standing still, baker. Jesus says, “the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.” The stars fall, and the powers of the heavens are shaken.

Mountains do show up earlier in this talk, friend, but not here. Jesus says, “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” He comes on the clouds of heaven, baker.

Temple gates, baker? I looked for a gate in that verse and came up empty-handed. Jesus says, “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” The clouds are the answer.
Prophets? I see the thinking, friend, but they aren't who He sends here. Jesus says, “And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call…” The angels are the answer, baker.
Disciples is a fair guess, friend, but they aren't who He sends. Jesus says, “And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call…” So the answer is angels.
That's backward from what Jesus says. He says, “As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.” Leaves sprouting, baker, not falling off.
Bending down isn't in the verse. Jesus says, “As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.” Tender branches and new leaves are the sign.
True. Jesus says, “Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.” Heaven and earth pass away, but His words don't. I'd stake my whole bakery on that, baker.
